subject.title: fix: protect SMS webhook callback quota [AI]

question: Should SMS webhook pre-authentication throttling be allowed to deny a later valid signed callback sharing the same account, route, and resolved client key?
rationale: If the denial is not mechanically removed, merging chooses a security-versus-message-availability policy that code review cannot safely infer.

options.title: Preserve signed delivery
options.body: Redesign the early defense so invalid traffic cannot consume admission capacity required by a later valid signed callback.

options.title: Accept fail-closed denial
options.body: Keep the early gate and explicitly document and prove that valid same-key callbacks may be rejected after hostile traffic.

recommendation.title: Preserve signed delivery
recommendation.body: Redesign the early defense so invalid traffic cannot consume admission capacity required by a later valid signed callback.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and recent history make steipete the strongest available routing candidate for this cross-cutting webhook policy choice.
